prediction.likelyOutcome: Metro is well positioned to win on liability — Brittany's admission that stopping rent was itself a breach, combined with the timeline showing Slyce's late oven disclosure (not Metro's delay) drove the floor-replacement issue, favors Metro on the central first-breach dispute. On damages, Metro's strongest and most collectible recovery is the $365,255 accrued-rent figure; the $327,626 Lump Sum Liquidated Damages claim functions as an alternative to, not an addition to, that figure and also faces a live penalty challenge, while the $135,113.88 construction-cost claim and $28,000 brokerage fee face real causation and speculation problems respectively. Net recovery against Slyce and its guarantors most likely lands in the $300,000-$400,000 range rather than the roughly $856,000 sum of every figure Metro's witness put into the record.

issues.label: Attorney's Fees Under Lease Fee-Shifting Clause

outcome.description: After a bench trial the court rejected the tenant's breach claim (and dismissed unjust enrichment), found the tenant and guarantors liable, and entered judgment for the landlord of $852,421.64: $365,255.76 rent, taxes and utilities through April 30, 2022; $111,910.38 construction expenses; $327,626.48 lump-sum liquidated damages; $28,000 brokerage fees; and $19,629.02 prejudgment interest. It later awarded $202,034.79 in attorney fees and costs without an evidentiary hearing. The Appellate Court affirmed liability and damages except the $28,000 brokerage fee, which it reversed, and reversed and remanded the fee award for an evidentiary hearing.
outcome.attorneysFeesOnAppeal: reversed and remanded for evidentiary hearing
outcome.finalNote: Affirmed except the $28,000 brokerage-fee component, which was reversed; fee award remanded.
